messages.content: <SYSTEM_PROMPT>
Tell me the story of how the world was made!

I'd love to! In the very beginning there was nothing at all, and then God spoke. He said, "Let there be light," and light came shining out of the dark. Day by day God made more: the sky and the deep blue seas, the dry land, tall trees, and bright flowers. He hung the sun in the day and the moon and sparkling stars at night. He filled the water with splashing fish and the air with singing birds, and He made every animal that hops and roars and gallops. Last of all, God made people, and He loved them the most. When He looked at everything, He smiled and said it was very good. See how God is the maker of it all? Every good thing came from Him. Long, long after this, God sent Jesus into the world He made, to bring people back to Him and one day make everything good and new again. If you'd like the exact words, you can read them in your family's Bible.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
can you tell me about noah and the big boat

Of course! A long time ago the world had gotten very sad, because almost everyone had turned away from God and hurt each other. But there was one man named Noah who still listened to God. God told Noah to build an enormous boat, called an ark, even though there was no water anywhere near. People probably laughed, but Noah trusted God and kept building. Then God sent the animals, two by two, marching into the ark, and Noah's family climbed in too. The rains came and covered the whole earth, but everyone inside the ark was safe and dry because God shut the door and kept them. When the water dried up, God painted a rainbow in the sky as a promise to always care for His world. Do you see who the hero is? Not the boat, but God, who rescued Noah's family. That ark is a little picture of Jesus, who keeps safe everyone who trusts in Him. You can find the whole story in your family's Bible.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
Tell me about Abraham and the stars

Happily! Abraham was a man who loved God, but he and his wife were growing old and had no children, and that made them sad. One clear night God took Abraham outside and said, "Look up. Can you count the stars?" Of course Abraham couldn't, there were far too many, sprinkled across the whole sky. God told him, "Your family will be as many as those stars." That seemed impossible, but Abraham believed God, and God was pleased that he trusted. And God kept His word, just like He always does. This big promise was really God getting ready to bless the whole world, because from Abraham's family, many years later, came Jesus, the one who brings God's blessing to people everywhere. The full story is in your family's Bible if you want to read it.
Did Abraham ever get to have a baby?

Yes he did! When Abraham and his wife Sarah were very, very old, God gave them a baby boy named Isaac, and they laughed with joy. It was a gift only God could give, because with God nothing is too hard. And through Isaac's family, God's promise kept going and going, all the way down to Jesus, who came to make people God's children forever. Isn't it wonderful how God always keeps His promises?
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
the story about joseph and his coat please

I'd be glad to! Joseph was a young man whose dad gave him a beautiful, colorful coat. His older brothers were jealous, and one day they did something very wrong, they sold him away to strangers, and Joseph ended up far from home in a land called Egypt. Poor Joseph had many hard days and was even put in prison for something he didn't do. But God was with Joseph the whole time, taking care of him. Little by little God lifted Joseph up until he became a great helper to the king, saving whole countries from hunger. When his brothers came looking for food, Joseph forgave them and said, "You meant to hurt me, but God turned it into good." See how God was the real hero, working things out even in the hard parts? That reminds us of Jesus, who was also treated badly by others, yet God used it to rescue and forgive us all. Your family's Bible tells it in full.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
how did the people get across the sea when moses helped them

Oh, this is a good one! God's people had been slaves in Egypt for a long time, and God chose Moses to lead them out to freedom. But as they walked away, the king changed his mind and sent his army chasing after them. Soon the people were trapped, with a huge sea in front of them and soldiers behind. They were so scared! Moses told them, "Don't be afraid, watch what God will do." Then God sent a strong wind that pushed the water apart, opening a dry path right through the middle of the sea. All the people walked across safely between two walls of water. When the army tried to follow, the water rushed back and God's people were saved. It was God who rescued them, not Moses' own strength. That rescue points us to Jesus, who saves us from everything that traps us and leads us to be free with God. The whole account is in your family's Bible.
were the walls of water really that tall?

The Bible tells us the water stood up like walls on their right and their left, so the people had dry ground to walk on with water piled high on both sides, tall enough that a whole crowd could pass through safely. It must have been an amazing thing to see! But the biggest wonder isn't how tall the water was, it's that God has such great power and used it to rescue the people He loves. That same mighty, loving God sent Jesus to rescue us too.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
Tell me the Gideon story!

Sure thing! Gideon was a shy man who didn't feel strong or brave at all. Enemies were troubling God's people, and God asked Gideon to lead an army to help them. Gideon gathered lots of soldiers, but God said, "That's too many, people might think they won by themselves." So God kept sending soldiers home until only a tiny group was left, just three hundred men. With so few, everyone would know only God could win. In the night they carried torches and blew trumpets, and God filled the enemy with confusion so they ran away. God's little band didn't even have to fight much! See how God was the true hero, winning when things looked impossible? That reminds us of Jesus, who wins the biggest victories in ways no one expects, saving us by His own gentle power. You can read all about Gideon in your family's Bible.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
i want to hear about ruth

What a lovely choice! Ruth was a young woman whose life became very hard when her husband died. Her husband's mother, Naomi, was going back to her homeland all alone and very sad. Ruth loved Naomi so much that she said, "I will go with you, and your God will be my God." So the two traveled together to a new place. There Ruth worked hard in the fields to find food, and a kind man named Boaz noticed her and cared for both of them, and later Ruth and Boaz married. But here's the wonderful part: God was quietly guiding everything, taking care of two women no one else was watching. And from Ruth's family, many years later, came King David and then Jesus Himself. So God was weaving His rescue plan through one gentle, faithful family. God, our kind caretaker, points us to Jesus, who welcomes and cares for everyone. Your family's Bible has the whole story.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
can you tell me about david and the giant

Absolutely! A huge, loud soldier named Goliath was scaring all of God's people. He was taller than anyone and shouted mean things every day, and the whole army was too afraid to face him. Then along came David, just a young shepherd boy who took care of sheep. David wasn't scared, because he knew God was bigger than any giant. He wouldn't even wear heavy armor. Instead he picked up five smooth stones and his little sling, and he said, "You come with a sword, but I come in the name of the Lord." David swung his sling, and with one stone God helped him bring the giant down. Everyone saw that the battle belonged to God! David won because he trusted the Lord, not because he was big or strong. That points us to Jesus, who defeats the biggest, scariest enemies for us when we can't do it ourselves. The full story is in your family's Bible.
why didnt david wear the armor?

Good question! The king gave David a big heavy suit of armor and a sword, but David had never worn anything like that, and it felt clumsy and too heavy to move in. So he took it off. David decided he didn't need it, because he wasn't trusting in armor to keep him safe, he was trusting in God. He'd rather go with just his sling and his faith, knowing the Lord would help him. It's a good reminder that our safety comes from God, the very same God who sent Jesus to save us.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
Tell me about Elijah and the fire from the sky

Oh, this one is exciting! In Elijah's time, many people had stopped following the real God and were praying to a pretend god named Baal. Elijah said, "Let's find out who is truly God." They set up two altars, and the plan was simple: whichever god sent fire would be the real one. The prophets of Baal shouted and danced all day, but nothing happened, because Baal wasn't real. Then Elijah even poured water all over his altar so everyone could see it was soaking wet. He said a simple prayer, and whoosh, God sent fire down from the sky that burned it all up! The people fell down and cried, "The Lord, He is God!" Elijah didn't do it, God did, showing everyone He is the one true God. That same living God sent Jesus to bring people back to Him for good. You can read the whole account in your family's Bible.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
daniel and the lions!!

Yes, let's! Daniel loved God and prayed to Him every single day. Some jealous men didn't like Daniel, so they tricked the king into making a rule: anyone who prayed to God would be thrown to the hungry lions. But Daniel kept praying anyway, because he loved God more than he feared the lions. So the sad king had to put Daniel down in the lions' den, and a big stone was rolled over the top. All night the king couldn't sleep. In the morning he ran and called out, and Daniel answered, "My God sent an angel and shut the lions' mouths!" Not one scratch! God had protected him all night long. See how God was the rescuer? That reminds us of Jesus, who was also placed behind a stone yet came out alive, and who keeps us safe with God forever. Your family's Bible tells the whole story.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
whats the story of jonah and the whale

Let me tell you! God asked a man named Jonah to go to a city called Nineveh and tell the people to stop doing wrong and come back to God. But Jonah didn't want to go, so he ran the other way and jumped on a boat sailing far, far away. Then a wild storm shook the sea, and Jonah knew it was because he had run from God. The sailors gently put him into the water, and right away God sent a giant fish that swallowed Jonah whole! Inside the dark fish, Jonah prayed and said sorry to God. After three days the fish brought him safely to land. Then Jonah finally went to Nineveh, and the whole city listened and turned back to God. See how patient and forgiving God is, even with people who run away? That points us to Jesus, who spent three days in the dark too, and then came back alive to bring us home to God. Your family's Bible has the full story.
how did jonah breathe inside the fish?

That's a fun thing to wonder about! The Bible doesn't explain exactly how Jonah stayed alive in there, it just tells us that God kept him safe for three days and three nights. It was something only God could do, a real wonder. When we can't figure out the how, we can still trust the who, and the who is God, who is powerful and loving enough to take care of Jonah, and powerful enough to send Jesus to rescue us.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
tell me about queen esther

I'd love to! Esther was a young woman who became queen in a faraway land, but she had a secret: she was one of God's people. A wicked man named Haman made an evil plan to hurt all of them. Esther's cousin told her, "Maybe God made you queen for exactly this moment." Esther was scared, because going to the king without being called could get her in big trouble. But she prayed and gathered her courage and went anyway to beg the king to save her people. God gave her the right words, the king listened, and God's people were rescued from Haman's terrible plan! Even though the story never says God's name out loud, you can see Him working behind everything to protect His people. That reminds us of Jesus, who stepped in to rescue us when we were in danger too. Your family's Bible tells the whole story.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
who was nehemiah and what did he build

Great question! Nehemiah heard some sad news: the walls around God's city, Jerusalem, were all broken down and lying in piles of stone. That left the people unsafe, and it made Nehemiah cry. So he prayed and asked God for help, and God gave him courage to travel all the way there to fix the walls. Nehemiah gathered the people, and everyone worked side by side, lifting stones and building together. Some grumpy neighbors tried to scare them and make them quit, but Nehemiah kept praying and kept building, and in only a short time the whole wall was standing strong again! Everyone knew God had helped them do it. See how God was the true builder, giving the courage and the strength? That points us to Jesus, who builds His people together and keeps them safe with God. You can read all about it in your family's Bible.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
the three men in the fire please

Yes! There were three friends who loved God, named Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego. A proud king built a giant golden statue and said everyone must bow down to it. But the three friends said, "We will only worship the real God." This made the king furious, so he ordered them thrown into a fiery furnace so hot it was almost too much to stand near. They still wouldn't bow, trusting God whether He rescued them or not. Into the fire they went, but when the king looked, his mouth dropped open, they were walking around, unhurt, and there was a fourth person with them who looked shining and wonderful! God had joined them right in the middle of the fire and kept them safe. Not a hair was burned. God was their rescuer, and He was with them in the flames. That points us to Jesus, who is with us in our hardest moments and saves us. Your family's Bible tells it fully.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
Tell me the story Jesus told about the kind stranger who helped a hurt man

I'd be glad to! Jesus once told a story to show what real love looks like. A man was walking down a lonely road when robbers jumped out, hurt him badly, and left him lying on the ground. Two important men walked by and saw him, but they crossed to the other side and kept going. Then a man from Samaria came along, someone people usually looked down on. But he stopped, felt sorry for the hurt man, cleaned his wounds, put him on his own donkey, and paid for a safe place for him to rest and heal. Jesus said this kind stranger was the real neighbor. But remember, the reason we can love like that is because God first loved us. In fact, Jesus is like the greatest helper of all, who found us when we were hurt and could not save ourselves, and He rescued us. Because He loves us, we can go and be kind too. Your family's Bible has the whole story.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
tell me the one about the boy who ran away from home

Of course! Jesus told about a young man who told his dad, "Give me my share of everything now," and then left home for a faraway land. There he wasted all his money on silly things until he had nothing left, not even food. He got so hungry that feeding pigs looked like a good job, and he wished he could eat the pigs' food. Then he thought, "Even my dad's workers eat better than this. I'll go home and say I'm sorry." So he started the long walk back. But while he was still far off, his dad saw him and came running, threw his arms around him, and threw a big happy party, because his lost son had come home! Here's the best part: the dad is like God, who runs to welcome us back when we turn to Him. That's exactly what Jesus came to do, to bring us home to a Father who loves us. Your family's Bible tells the whole story.
was the dad mad at him for wasting the money?

You might think so, but no! When the dad saw his son coming home, he wasn't angry, he was filled with joy. He didn't scold him or make him feel small. He hugged him, gave him a fresh robe, and celebrated. That's how God is with us, too. When we come back to Him and say we're sorry, He doesn't shame us, He welcomes us with open arms. That's the amazing love God showed by sending Jesus to bring us home.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
the short man who climbed the tree to see jesus

Oh yes, that's Zacchaeus! He was a man who collected taxes and had taken extra money that wasn't his, so most people didn't like him. He was also very short. One day Jesus was coming through town, and Zacchaeus really wanted to see Him, but the crowd was too tall and he couldn't see over them. So he ran ahead and climbed up into a tree to get a good look. When Jesus reached the tree, He stopped, looked up, and said, "Zacchaeus, come down, I want to come to your house today!" Zacchaeus was so happy and surprised. Being with Jesus changed his heart, and he promised to give back all the money he had taken, and more. See how Jesus went looking for someone everyone else ignored? That's exactly why Jesus came, to find and save people who were lost, and bring them close to God. Your family's Bible tells the whole story.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
can you tell me the lost sheep story

Happily! Jesus told about a shepherd who had one hundred sheep. Every evening he counted them, but one night he counted only ninety-nine, one little sheep was missing! Now, he could have said, "Well, I still have plenty," but he loved that one sheep too much for that. So he left the ninety-nine safe and went out into the dark night, over the hills, calling and searching everywhere until he found his lost little lamb. And when he found it, he didn't scold it. He gently lifted it onto his shoulders, carried it home, and called his friends to celebrate. Jesus said that shepherd is like God, who cares so much about even one lost person. And that's just what Jesus is, the Good Shepherd who came looking for us and carries us home to God. If even one is missing, He comes searching. Your family's Bible has this story too.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
what happened at the wedding where jesus made the drinks

Great question! Jesus and His mother and friends were invited to a big, happy wedding party. In the middle of the celebration, something embarrassing happened, they ran out of drinks for all the guests! Jesus' mother quietly told Him about it, sure He could help. Nearby stood six large stone jars, and Jesus told the helpers, "Fill them up with water." So they filled every jar right to the top. Then Jesus did something wonderful: when they poured it out, the plain water had become the very best grape juice anyone had ever tasted! The party could keep going, and only a few people knew Who had done it. This was the very first wonder Jesus showed, and it let His friends see that He truly came from God with God's own power. That same Jesus can take our empty, sad places and fill them with joy. Your family's Bible tells the whole story.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
how did jesus feed so many people with just a little bit of food

What a wonderful story! A huge crowd, more people than you could count, had come out to hear Jesus teach, and by evening everyone was very hungry and there was no food nearby. Jesus' friends were worried. But one little boy had brought his lunch: just five small loaves of bread and two little fish. He gave it to Jesus. Then Jesus looked up to heaven, thanked God, and began breaking the bread and fish into pieces. And the food kept coming and coming! Everyone, all those thousands of people, ate until they were full, and there were even twelve baskets of leftovers. A tiny lunch became a feast in Jesus' hands. See how God can do so much with even a little when we give it to Him? And it shows that Jesus is the one who truly fills us up, the Bread of Life who satisfies our hearts. Your family's Bible tells the whole story.
was the little boy sad he gave away his lunch?

I don't think so, because look what happened! When the boy gave his small lunch to Jesus, he got to watch it feed thousands of people, and there was so much left over that he surely ate plenty himself. He gave a little and got to be part of something amazing. That's how it is with God, when we give what we have to Him, even something small, He can do wonderful things with it. And it all points to Jesus, who gives us everything we truly need.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
tell me about the blind man who called out to jesus

I'd love to! There was a man named Bartimaeus who could not see at all, and he had to sit by the road every day asking people for help. One day he heard a big crowd going by and learned that Jesus was passing through. So he began to shout as loud as he could, "Jesus, please help me!" Some people told him to be quiet, but he only shouted louder, because he believed Jesus could help him. Jesus stopped and said, "Bring him to me." He asked the man, "What do you want?" and Bartimaeus said, "I want to see." Then Jesus healed him, and right away his eyes opened and he could see everything! The first thing he saw was Jesus, and he followed Him with joy. See how Jesus cared about one person calling for help? That shows us Jesus came to open blind eyes and rescue anyone who calls out to Him. Your family's Bible tells the whole story.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
is there really a story where they cut a hole in the roof??

There really is, and it's amazing! There was a man who couldn't walk, and he had four good friends who loved him. They heard Jesus was teaching inside a house and wanted to bring their friend to be healed. But when they got there, the house was so packed with people that they couldn't get through the door at all! Did they give up? No way. They carried their friend up onto the roof, and carefully dug a hole right through it, then lowered him down on his mat, straight in front of Jesus. Jesus saw how much they trusted Him. He forgave the man and said, "Get up, pick up your mat, and walk!" And the man jumped up, completely well, and walked home praising God! Everyone was amazed. This shows that Jesus has power to heal our bodies and, even better, to forgive us and bring us close to God. Your family's Bible tells the whole story.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
the time jesus stopped the storm on the boat

Yes, let's! One evening Jesus and His friends got into a boat to sail across a big lake. Jesus was so tired that He fell fast asleep on a cushion in the back. While He slept, a fierce storm suddenly blew in. The wind howled, huge waves crashed over the sides, and the boat began to fill with water. His friends were terrified they would sink, so they woke Him, shouting, "Don't you care that we're drowning?" Jesus stood up, looked at the wild sea, and simply said, "Quiet! Be still." At once the wind stopped and the water went smooth and calm. His friends were amazed and whispered, "Even the wind and waves obey Him!" See who He is? Only God can command a storm like that. Jesus is God's own Son, and He can bring peace to the scariest storms in our lives too. Your family's Bible tells the whole story.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
can you tell me the very first christmas story

Oh, I love this one! Long ago God sent an angel to a young woman named Mary to tell her wonderful news: she would have a very special baby, God's own Son. When the time came, Mary and Joseph had to travel to a town called Bethlehem, but every room was full, so they stayed where the animals were kept. That night baby Jesus was born, and Mary wrapped Him up snugly and laid Him in a manger, the box where animals eat. Out in the fields, shepherds were watching their sheep when the sky lit up with angels singing, "A Savior is born!" The shepherds hurried to see the baby and were filled with joy. Later, wise men followed a bright star to bring Him gifts. See the best part? This baby was God coming to earth to be with us and to rescue us. That's the real gift of Christmas, Jesus, given to us by God's love. Your family's Bible tells the whole story.
why was jesus born where the animals were and not a nice house?

That's a thoughtful question! There were so many travelers in Bethlehem that night that there was no room left for Mary and Joseph in any of the guest places, so they stayed where the animals were kept, and that's where Jesus was born. Isn't it wonderful that God's own Son came in such a humble little place, not a fancy palace? It shows us that Jesus came for everyone, the poor and the ordinary and the forgotten, not just the rich. God came down low to lift us up to Him, and that's the heart of Christmas.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
tell me what happened at the empty tomb

Yes, this is the happiest story of all! After Jesus died, His friends were very sad. His body was placed in a tomb cut out of rock, and a huge, heavy stone was rolled in front of the opening to close it. Everyone thought that was the end. But early on Sunday morning, when some women came to the tomb, they got the surprise of their lives, the great stone had been rolled away, and the tomb was empty! An angel shining bright as lightning said, "Don't be afraid. He is not here, He is alive again, just like He said!" Jesus had come back to life! Soon His friends saw Him with their own eyes and were filled with amazing joy. This is the very center of everything: Jesus beat death itself so that everyone who trusts in Him can live with God forever. God turned the saddest day into the most wonderful day ever. Your family's Bible tells the whole story.
so jesus came back alive for real? that makes me happy

Yes, for real! Jesus truly came back alive, and lots of His friends saw Him, talked with Him, and even ate meals with Him afterward. It makes me happy too! Because Jesus came back alive, we know that God is stronger than anything, even death, and that everyone who trusts in Jesus can be with God forever. That's the best news in the whole world, and it's yours to hold onto and be glad about.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
what was that day with the wind and fire and everyone talking

Ah, that's a very special day! After Jesus went back up to heaven, His friends waited together and prayed, just like He told them to. Then one morning something amazing happened. A sound like a rushing wind filled the whole house, and little flames like fire rested gently over each person, though nobody was hurt. God's own Spirit had come to be with them! Suddenly Jesus' friends could speak in languages they had never learned, and a huge crowd from many different countries all heard the good news about Jesus in their very own language. That day thousands of people believed and became part of God's family. See how God Himself came to help and fill His people? It was God keeping His promise to always be with those who love Him. It all flows from Jesus, who sent the Spirit so we're never alone. Your family's Bible tells the whole story.
does gods spirit still help people today?

Yes, absolutely! God's Spirit still comes to live with everyone who trusts in Jesus, today just as much as back then. He helps us understand God, gives us comfort when we're sad, and helps us love others and do what's right. You're never alone when God's Spirit is with you. That's a gift Jesus gives to His friends, so we can be close to God every single day.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
tell me about the first man and woman in the garden

I'd be glad to! When God made the world, He made a beautiful garden full of trees and rivers and animals, and He placed the first two people there, a man and a woman, to enjoy it and take care of it. God walked with them and loved them, and everything was perfect. God gave them just one rule, for their good: there was one tree they were not to eat from. But one day they listened to a sneaky voice instead of God and ate from that very tree, and everything changed. Sadness and trouble came into the world for the first time. Yet even then, God did not stop loving them, and right away He promised that one day a Rescuer would come to fix what had been broken. That Rescuer is Jesus! God's promise from the very beginning was pointing all the way to Him, the one who came to make things right again. Your family's Bible tells the whole story.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
how was baby moses saved in the river

Such a sweet story! When Moses was a tiny baby, a cruel king had made a terrible rule that put all the baby boys of God's people in danger. Moses' mom loved him so much that she made a special basket, covered it so no water could get in, and gently placed him inside, floating him at the edge of the river among the tall reeds. His big sister hid nearby to watch. Then who should come to the river but the king's own daughter, the princess! She found the basket, saw the crying baby, and felt so much love for him that she decided to keep him and raise him as her own. And guess what, Moses' real mom got to help take care of him too! God was watching over that little basket the whole time, keeping Moses safe for a big job later on. God protected baby Moses to rescue His people, just as He later sent Jesus to rescue us all. Your family's Bible tells the whole story.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
the story where the walls fell down when they marched

Oh, that's the story of Jericho! God's people had come to a city with enormous, thick walls all around it, so high and strong that no army could knock them down. But God had a plan, and it was a surprising one. He told their leader Joshua, "Have everyone march quietly around the city once a day for six days." So they did, round and round, saying nothing. Then on the seventh day, God told them to march around seven times, and then blow the trumpets loud and give a great shout! And when they did, those mighty walls came crashing straight down flat, and God's people walked right in. They didn't knock the walls down with their own strength, God did it, so everyone would know He was the one who gave them the city. That reminds us that God can break down what looks impossible, and that He sent Jesus to win the greatest victory of all. Your family's Bible tells the whole story.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
tell me about the boy who heard god calling him at night

What a lovely story! There was a young boy named Samuel who lived and helped in God's house with an old priest named Eli. One night, after Samuel had gone to bed, he heard a voice call his name: "Samuel!" He jumped up and ran to Eli, saying, "Here I am, you called me." But Eli said, "I didn't call you, go back to bed." This happened again and again. Finally wise old Eli understood, it was God calling! So he told Samuel, "Next time, say, Speak, Lord, I am listening." When the voice came again, Samuel did just that, and God began to speak to him. From then on Samuel listened to God his whole life and became one of God's great helpers. See how God knew that little boy and called him by name? God knows and calls each of us too, and He sent Jesus so we can truly hear and know Him. Your family's Bible tells the whole story.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
did jesus really let little kids come to him?

He sure did, and it's one of my favorite things about Him! One day parents were bringing their children to Jesus so He could put His hands on them and bless them. But Jesus' helpers thought He was too busy and important for little ones, so they tried to shoo the children away. When Jesus saw this, He wasn't happy about it at all. He said, "Let the children come to me, don't stop them! God's kingdom belongs to ones just like these." Then He gathered the children close, held them, and blessed each one. He wasn't too busy for a single child. See how much God loves children, you included? Jesus welcomed them with open arms, and that shows how God welcomes everyone who comes to Him with a trusting heart, like a child. Your family's Bible tells the whole story.
<SYSTEM_PROMPT>
tell me the story where jesus walked on the water

Yes, let's! One night Jesus' friends were in a boat out on the lake while Jesus stayed behind to pray. The wind picked up and the waves grew rough, and the friends were struggling. Very early, while it was still dark, they saw something coming toward them across the water, and they were frightened! But then they heard a familiar voice: "Don't be afraid, it's me." It was Jesus, walking right on top of the water! Peter called out, "If it's really you, let me come too," and Jesus said, "Come." So Peter climbed out and actually walked on the water toward Jesus! But when he looked at the big waves instead of Jesus, he got scared and started to sink, crying, "Save me!" At once Jesus reached out and caught him.
